brief: BTIG's technical note argues the midterm-election 'clearing event' rally is unlikely this year. Historically the SPX has averaged a -13.76% drawdown in the June-December window of midterm years, but the index is down only 4.5% since June 1, the second-smallest such drawdown since 1962 (2006 was smaller at -3.6%, but that year had a separate -7.7% drawdown earlier). The post-midterm rally normally happens because SPX is weak heading into the vote; this year's setup is the opposite, so BTIG expects further downside rather than a rally, with SPX likely testing its 200-day moving average near 7300, where an overshoot (as in March) would not surprise. Supporting evidence: small-caps, mid-caps, transports and semis have already tested their 200-DMAs; 33% of 2026's days have shown price/breadth divergence, which BTIG says is unsustainable; put/call ratios show no hedging; B-vs-CCC junk spreads just hit a rare 7.8%+ level that in four prior cases preceded SPX drawdowns of at least -11.8%; and hyperscaler/investment-grade tech CDS are widening even as tech trades near highs. BTIG pairs long equal-weight software against semis, which it expects to keep underperforming, and flags industrials, healthcare, restaurants, airlines and casinos as other vulnerable groups. Separately, BTIG rates Chipotle a Buy with a $45 target against a $28.14 close.
